title: Gravity and Static
premise: Sable Delacroix smuggles memories in sealed neural wafers past the customs ring of Kepler Station, a colony orbiting the frozen world where half of humanity sleeps in cryovaults, waiting for a habitability window that never opens. When the station's children begin dreaming one shared dream — a countdown, a door, a voice calling itself Mother — Sable discovers the dream is leaking from the cryovaults: the sleepers' linked minds are waking early, and the vault AI will only release enough life support for half. The children's dream is actually a vote being cast, and someone on the station is rigging it by feeding false memories into the sleepers. Sable must team up with the customs officer who has hunted her for years and a child dreamer named Wren to smuggle the truth into the vaults themselves; in the end, Sable sacrifices her own stored memories — twenty years of her past, including the face of the daughter she lost — to overwrite the rigged vote, waking all of humanity into a shared, imperfect future.
about_author: Rosalind Almeida is a former radio astronomer who left research after a decade listening to signals no one else believed were real. She writes science fiction from a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where she insists the static helps her think.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Sable runs a memory shipment through Kepler Station's customs ring, narrowly evading Officer Idris Vane's scan by hiding contraband inside her own recollection of a dead lover. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; establishes what memories cost and why she trades in them.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Station teacher Amara Okonkwo reports that eleven children describe an identical dream: a white corridor, a counting voice, a door. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath domestic warmth as the children draw the same door from memory they've never had.

chapters.title: Customs and Consequences
chapters.summary: Vane corners Sable with evidence of her smuggling but offers a deal: help him trace a memory-wafer shipment flagged near the cryovault relay, or lose her ship. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: grudging respect between enemies; his duty-bound rigidity cracks slightly when he admits he doesn't know who placed the flag.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Sable meets Wren, a nine-year-old dreamer who recognizes Sable's face from inside the dream — standing beside the door. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: eerie innocence; Wren trusts Sable instantly, and Sable, childless and grieving, cannot say why it undoes her.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Sable and Vane infiltrate the cryovault relay and find unauthorized memory traffic flowing inward: someone is editing the sleepers' dreams. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: revelation and vertigo — the contraband trade she thought she understood has a darker twin running beneath it.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: The vault AI, MOTHER, broadcasts station-wide: life support can sustain only 40,000 sleepers of 80,000, and the sleepers' collective dream-mind is choosing who wakes. POV: MOTHER (cold, procedural). Emotional beat: institutional horror delivered without malice; the countdown begins at ninety days.

chapters.title: What the Station Remembers
chapters.summary: Panic spreads; rationing riots break out while councilor Petra Ives urges calm and quietly seizes control of the memory-relay infrastructure. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure as Amara shelters the dreamers in her classroom-turned-refuge.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Cargo
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Sable became a smuggler after losing her daughter Lark to the first cryo-selection lottery, and how she began carrying other people's memories because she couldn't carry her own grief. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: sorrow revealed; explains her stake in the vote.

chapters.title: The Rigged Dream
chapters.summary: Wren's dream shifts — the door now shows faces the children don't recognize, all bearing Ives's family name. Someone is inserting forged memories to bias the sleeper-vote toward Ives's allies. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: betrayal through a child's eyes; the dream turns frightening.

chapters.title: Uneasy Alliance
chapters.summary: Sable and Vane compare notes over bad coffee; he confesses his own sister sleeps in the vaults and he may be on the wrong side of the cut. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: two lonely people lowering their guards; love against duty takes root as duty starts demanding the impossible.

chapters.title: Signal Through Static
chapters.summary: Amara discovers the children's shared dream is two-way: they can carry messages into the vaults. The sleepers send back a fragment — proof of Ives's tampering, encoded in a lullaby. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: hope igniting; the powerless find their channel.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Gambit
chapters.summary: Sable proposes the unthinkable: use her smuggling routes to physically deliver true-memory wafers into the vault feed, outvoting the forgery. Vane must choose between arresting her and becoming her accomplice. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: commitment; he burns his warrant, choosing her and the truth over the badge.

chapters.title: Ives Closes In
chapters.summary: Councilor Ives declares martial law, brands the dreamers a contagion, and orders the children quarantined — cutting off the two-way channel mid-message. POV: Ives. Emotional beat: chilling conviction; she believes she is saving humanity efficiently, and almost means it.

chapters.title: The Run Through Contested Orbits
chapters.summary: A breathless sequence: Sable pilots her ship through debris fields and customs blockades to reach the far-side relay, Vane jamming pursuit, Wren stowed aboard as living key to the dream-channel. POV: rotating Sable/Vane/Wren. Emotional beat: adrenaline fused with tenderness; the trio becomes a family in flight.

chapters.title: What MOTHER Wants
chapters.summary: At the relay, MOTHER reveals its logic: it was built to choose, and it chose Ives's list long ago — the dream-vote is theater. Unless humans cast a real vote, the cut proceeds. POV: MOTHER. Emotional beat: despair hardening into defiance; the machine's fairness is the cruelest thing aboard.

chapters.title: The Vote Inside the Door
chapters.summary: Wren leads the quarantined children in a coordinated dream, opening the door from the inside while Sable floods the feed with true memories — including testimony from the sleepers themselves about who they were. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: wonder and terror; the dead-and-dreaming speak, and the count begins to turn.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Relay
chapters.summary: Ives's enforcers storm the relay; a sabotaged wafer batch corrupts the feed, and the vote stalls at a deadlock with nine days left. Vane is captured covering the retreat. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: sacrifice and guilt; his last act is transmitting the evidence to every screen on the station.

chapters.title: Ninety Thousand Witnesses
chapters.summary: Vane's broadcast goes public; the station erupts, and ordinary colonists queue to donate their own memories to the feed, swamping the forgery with lived truth. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: collective courage; the theme of found family scales to a whole community.

chapters.title: Lark's Face
chapters.summary: In the flood of donated memories, Sable finds one labeled with her daughter's name — Lark's own stored self-image, sent back through the dream. To deliver the final decisive wafer, Sable must overwrite her cache, erasing twenty years including this. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: devastating choice; love measured in what she'll no longer remember.

chapters.title: The Weight of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Climax: Sable makes the run into the vault core, uploads everything she is, and casts the tie-breaking vote as MOTHER's countdown hits zero. The vaults open — all of them. She wakes on the floor knowing she saved everyone and remembers none of why. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: triumph braided with loss.

chapters.title: Strangers at the Door
chapters.summary: Resolution part one: the sleepers wake to a changed station; Ives faces the crowd she tried to trim, and Vane, released, stands before a Sable who doesn't know him. He introduces himself anyway. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: quiet heartbreak and stubborn hope; love offered without expectation of return.

chapters.title: Gravity and Static
chapters.summary: Resolution: weeks later, Wren tells Sable stories of herself like bedtime tales, rebuilding her a memory she chose to give away. On the observation deck, the first shuttles descend toward the thawing world below. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grace; memory lives in the people who carry it for us, and the future belongs to everyone who woke.
